subject: Bluehaven.ai — Quick ask: per-1M IO rates and supported models
messages:
From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@bluehaven.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + quick pricing ask

Hi Marissa,

Nice to meet you — I'm Ethan (Head of Product at Bluehaven.ai). We're evaluating vendors for embedded LLM features (summarization + search relevance). Before we schedule a demo, could you share Redwood's standard hosted API IO rates on a per-1M token basis (separate input vs output if applicable) and a simple list of supported models / tiers (small, medium, large equivalents)?

Also: do you publish volume discount tiers or standard discounts for startups in Series A/B? I've attached a short RFP overview (bluehaven_RFP_details.pdf) with expected traffic (roughly 10M tokens/month initial, ramp to ~100M in 6 months).

Thanks — a short bullet reply is perfect.

—Ethan
Ethan Ross
Head of Product, Bluehaven.ai
attachment: bluehaven_RFP_details.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + quick pricing ask

Hi Ethan — great to meet you, and thanks for the RFP. Short answer below; happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through specifics.

Baseline hosted API IO rates (per 1M tokens):
- Input tokens: $0.80 per 1M tokens
- Output tokens: $1.50 per 1M tokens

Model tiers (hosted catalog):
- small: rdm-small (good for instruction-following & low latency; lower cost)
- medium: rdm-medium (balanced quality/latency)
- large: rdm-large (best quality for long-form generation)
- specialized: rdm-chat and rdm-embed variants (chat-optimized, embeddings)

Volume discounts: standard tiered discounts kick in at committed monthly volumes: 50M (5% off), 200M (12%), 500M+ (20%). We also run time-limited trial credits for new integrations.

I attached our standard ratecard PDF for reference. If you share a target commit range, I can return a tailored quote.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick thoughts:

- IO rates: we price per-1M tokens uniformly across small/medium tiers but add a model-surcharge for rdm-large and specialized models (typically +25% on output rate for rdm-large / fine-tuned variants). That keeps pricing simple while reflecting cost delta.
- Discounts: applied to combined billable IO (sum of input + output). For committed annual prepay we can be more aggressive: 12-month prepay at 20% off list for 100M+ average monthly usage is reasonable to offer (requires approval for startup tier).
- Proposal: give them a staged commit proposal: Month 1-3 at list (or mild 5% off), Month 4-6 scale to 50M/m with 8–10% off, Month 7+ at 100M/m with 15–20% off if they prepay. Include an escape clause if usage underperforms.

If Bluehaven wants a firm quote, we should ask for an expected model mix (%% small/medium/large + embedding calls) to be precise.

—Ben (cc: Laura)
Ben Carter
Lead Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ethan — thanks for the quick replies and context. Based on your RFP and our internal review, here's a concise suggested path you can use in financial planning. I've attached the standard ratecard for reference and included a simple staged-commit proposal below.

Suggested staged-commit quote (hosted API, per-1M IO):
- List (all models small/medium baseline): Input $0.80 / 1M, Output $1.50 / 1M
- rdm-large surcharge (output): +25% (output becomes $1.875 / 1M when rdm-large is used)

Staged discount schedule (applies to combined IO):
- Months 1–3: pilot — list pricing (or 5% on a 3-month prepay)
- Months 4–6: scale to 50M/mo — 8% discount on combined IO
- Months 7–12: target 100M/mo — 15% discount on combined IO (20% available if Bluehaven prepays full 12 months upfront)

Notes / next steps:
- If you can share expected model mix (approx %% small/medium/large and expected embedding calls), Ben can run a one-page TCO showing monthly cost under the staged proposal.
- We can convert the outline into a formal commercial term sheet if you want to proceed; typical turnaround is 2–3 business days.
- I've attached: redwood_standard_ratecard_v2.pdf and included a calendar link if you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough.

Would you like Ben to pull together the TCO with a model-mix assumption? If so, share the mix and preferred commit (monthly vs prepay).

Best,
Marissa Cole
